claims.text: FeNiCrMn is a Co-free derivative of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Removing Co lowers the intrinsic stacking-fault energy of FeNiCrMn relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
At 293–500 K and strain rates of at least 10^-3 s^-1, the reduced stacking-fault energy promotes deformation twinning.
Deformation twinning is the dominant plasticity mechanism for FeNiCrMn within the proposed regime.
Twinning produces enhanced strain hardening in FeNiCrMn relative to CoCrFeMnNi.
Twinning allows FeNiCrMn to retain greater ductility than CoCrFeMnNi under dynamic tensile loading.
The proposed FeNiCrMn specimens are homogenized, fully FCC, equiaxed-grained solid solutions with an approximately 10 μm grain size.
Lower stacking-fault energy increases the critical stress for dislocation cross-slip relative to the stress for twinning.
The relative suppression of cross-slip shifts plasticity toward twinning-induced plasticity.
Twinning-induced plasticity sustains work hardening at high strain rates.
FeNiCrMn will have at least a 15% higher strain-hardening rate than CoCrFeMnNi under identical loading.
FeNiCrMn will have at least a 10% greater deformation-twin volume fraction than CoCrFeMnNi under identical loading.
FeNiCrMn will have a higher strain-rate sensitivity coefficient than CoCrFeMnNi.
The mechanism applies only to fully FCC solid-solution material at 293–500 K, strain rates of 10^-3–10^3 s^-1, and grain sizes of 5–20 μm.
The proposed mechanism does not apply to phase-transformed or precipitate-strengthened states.
Matched testing at 293 K and strain rates of 10^-3 and 10^2 s^-1, followed by EBSD or TEM measurement of twins at approximately 20% strain, can distinguish the proposed twinning mechanism.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires at least a 10% greater twin volume fraction, whereas the falsification rule requires more than 10%; an exactly 10% increase would satisfy the prediction but fail the stated falsification threshold.

The hypothesis identifies dominant twinning as the central mechanism, but the falsification rule is phrased conjunctively so that failure to increase twinning may not falsify the mechanism unless the strain-hardening-rate and strain-rate-sensitivity criteria also fail.
